## Conservation laws and stage ordering (`none`) {#sec-ch02-laws}

### Summary

snapy advances cell averages of mass, momentum and energy. Each stage turns face fluxes into a change of every
cell, adds the sources, and then hands the result to the time integrator. The one property this section owns is
that mass, momentum and energy only move between cells: a face flux leaves one cell and enters its neighbour with
the same value, so the sum over the domain changes only through the outer faces. The section also fixes where in
the last stage the phase adjustment sits, because that decides what the wall ghost cells see.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Forms the flux-only stage increment, @eq-ch02-laws-increment, whose volume-weighted sum telescopes.

**Data.** Reads face fluxes, face areas, cell volumes $V_i$[^rg-6dfd3fd44de6] and $\Delta t$[^rg-6e8706cff990]; writes the stage increment `du`.

**Placement.** Every RK[^rg-f31b5cad787a] stage, in `HydroImpl::forward`; the phase solve and boundary fill end the last stage.

**Activation.** Always on; no switch. The integrator sets the number of stages.

**Guarantee / limits.** Interior faces cancel exactly in exact arithmetic; round-off below $\tfrac32\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\Delta t\sum_i\lvert\Delta_i[A\mathbf F_1]\rvert$.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch02-laws-tests: one ctest by source reading, `laws_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C3]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\Delta\mathbf U^{\mathrm{flux}}_i$ the flux-only increment of
cell $i$[^rg-9fe3deae45f9]; $A_{i+1/2}$ the area of face $i+1/2$ [m$^2$]; $[A\mathbf F_1]_{i+1/2}=A_{i+1/2}\mathbf F_{1,i+1/2}$ the face product,
area times flux [units of $\mathbf U$[^rg-8ef399e5745d] times m$^3$ s$^{-1}$]; $\eta_j$ the relative error of one rounding.

### Derivation

#### From the conservation law to the flux-only increment

Density $\rho$[^rg-549e5380ddb0] is in kg m$^{-3}$, momentum density $m_a$ in kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ and total energy density $E$[^rg-360f6f825688] in
J m$^{-3}$. On the nonorthogonal grid the primitive velocities are contravariant and the conserved momenta
covariant. Dry density and every species partial density obey their own continuity equation; their sum is total
continuity. For an inviscid Cartesian cell without phase change,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm d}+\boldsymbol\nabla\cdot(\rho_{\mathrm d}\mathbf v)&=0,\\
\partial_t\rho_n+\boldsymbol\nabla\cdot(\rho_n\mathbf v)&=0,\\
\partial_t\mathbf m+\boldsymbol\nabla\cdot(\mathbf m\mathbf v+p\mathsf I)&=\rho\mathbf g,\\
\partial_t E+\boldsymbol\nabla\cdot[(E+p)\mathbf v]&=\rho\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf g.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\mathbf g=(g_1,g_2,g_3)$ is the acceleration in m s$^{-2}$. Coriolis, diffusion and the configured sources
add their own terms (@sec-ch09); the geometric momentum terms enter through the coordinate operator (@sec-ch03).

The equations above keep the full vertical momentum equation, so the vertical velocity is prognostic and sound
waves are resolved; the explicit step is then bounded by the acoustic time-step limit (@sec-ch07-cfl) unless the
vertically implicit correction removes it in $x_1$[^rg-88d9f77d83d1] (@sec-ch07-vic-options). A side-by-side list of the
differences from a hydrostatic primitive-equation core is answered at @sec-ch02-pecore.

The flux-only increment follows in three steps.

1. *Integrate over a fixed cell.* The cell does not move, so the time derivative passes outside the integral and
   gives $V_i\,\mathrm d\mathbf U_i/\mathrm dt$ for the cell average $\mathbf U_i$.
2. *Turn the divergence into faces.* Gauss's theorem makes the volume integral of $\boldsymbol\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$
   the outward flux through the faces. The scheme replaces each face integral by the face area times one numerical
   flux, giving the face product $[A\mathbf F_1]_{i+1/2}$.
3. *Multiply by $\Delta t$ and divide by $V_i$.* With only the $x_1$ faces written out, this is

$$
\Delta\mathbf U^{\mathrm{flux}}_i=-\frac{\Delta t}{V_i}\Delta_i[A\mathbf F_1]
$$ {#eq-ch02-laws-increment}

with $\Delta_i[A\mathbf F_1]=[A\mathbf F_1]_{i+1/2}-[A\mathbf F_1]_{i-1/2}$. @eq-ch02-laws-increment is built in `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) from the divergence of
`CoordinateImpl::divergence` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}).

#### Why the sum over cells telescopes

1. *The same number on both sides of a face.* `CoordinateImpl::divergence` forms the face products twice, once
   for the right faces of all cells and once for the left faces (the excerpt in the Code layer). For face $i+1/2$
   the two products, in cell $i$ and in cell $i+1$, multiply the same area element by the same flux element: both
   `face_area1` calls slice one element-wise formula on the same grid tensors
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl::face_area1 >}}), and both flux slices read one tensor. IEEE multiplication is correctly rounded, so identical operands give identical products, bit for bit.
   Cell $i$ subtracts that number and cell $i+1$ adds it.
2. *Weight by volume and sum.* $\sum_iV_i\Delta\mathbf U^{\mathrm{flux}}_i=-\Delta t\sum_i\Delta_i[A\mathbf F_1]$.
3. *Interior faces cancel.* Let $N$ be the number of cells in this column. Every interior face product
   appears once with each sign, so the sum is
   $-\Delta t([A\mathbf F_1]_{N+1/2}-[A\mathbf F_1]_{1/2})$: only the outer faces remain.
4. *Hence conservation is algebra, not accuracy.* The cancellation needs only that both neighbours use the same
   number; how accurate that flux is belongs to @sec-ch04.

Round-off is where the identity can fail. One rounding returns $\mathrm{fl}(a\circ b)=(a\circ b)(1+\eta_j)$ with
$\lvert\eta_j\rvert\le\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2$, where $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=2^{-52}$ in double precision. Each cell
rounds three times: the face difference, the division by $V_i$ and the product with $-\Delta t$ (the negation is
exact). So the computed increment is

$$
\widehat{\Delta\mathbf U}{}^{\mathrm{flux}}_i
=-\frac{\Delta t}{V_i}\,\Delta_i[A\mathbf F_1]\,(1+\eta_1)(1+\eta_2)(1+\eta_3).
$$

The rounding of each face product carries no error into the sum: by step 1 both neighbours hold the same
rounded number, so it cancels exactly.
Subtract the exact increment, drop the products of two rounding errors, multiply by $V_i$ and sum:

$$
\Bigl\lvert\sum_iV_i\widehat{\Delta\mathbf U}{}^{\mathrm{flux}}_i+\Delta t\,([A\mathbf F_1]_{N+1/2}-[A\mathbf F_1]_{1/2})\Bigr\rvert
\le\tfrac32\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,\Delta t\sum_i\bigl\lvert\Delta_i[A\mathbf F_1]\bigr\rvert .
$$

The defect scales with the face differences, not with the size of the state, so a nearly uniform flux field
conserves to well below one unit in the last place of the domain total.

#### Why the phase adjustment comes before the wall fill

Phase adjustment changes the interior composition after transport. A wall ghost copied before the adjustment
keeps the pre-adjustment composition, and the reconstruction of the next stage sees a jump that the interior does not have.
Copying afterwards makes the reflected thermodynamic state equal to the adjusted interior again. The code does it
in that order: the last `apply_boundaries` call of `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` follows the saturation block
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch02-laws-flow shows one stage. `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` runs it in this order:

1. `HydroImpl::forward`: reconstruct face states, solve the Riemann problems, limit the fluxes, form the divergence
   `_div`, start `du` from $-\Delta t$ times `_div` on interior cells, add the forcing modules (@sec-ch09) and the
   vertical implicit correction if it is on (@sec-ch07);
2. the user stage forcings, after `HydroImpl::forward` returns;
3. the RK averaging of `pintg->forward` and the conserved limiter;
4. the solid refill, if there are solids;
5. on the last stage only: the phase adjustment (@sec-ch02-saturation) when the thermo carries reactions, then the
   gravity-work fixer when it is on (@sec-ch06);
6. `apply_boundaries`, which fills the physical ghosts.

The EOS conversions inside these steps have no spatial stencil. Ghost exchange and seam flux agreement belong to
@sec-ch03 and @sec-ch07.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Transport produces a flux increment before forcing, phase adjustment and physical ghost filling."
#| fig-alt: "Transport produces a flux increment before forcing, phase adjustment and physical ghost filling."
#| echo: false
```

### Code

**A minimal input.** The laws have no switch; any deck runs them. This one is the wall-saturation test deck
without its species, reduced to the keys that set the stage:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dynamics`[^rg-e0f7416a96dd], `equation-of-state`[^rg-40c7b90c688a], `reconstruct`[^rg-f601adb778fa], `vertical`[^rg-24c421484b56], `horizontal`[^rg-578716044c42], `riemann-solver`[^rg-b4a63e1af281], `integration`[^rg-db8b48077d05], `cfl`[^rg-7b32cac9c821].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-gas}
  reconstruct:
    vertical: {type: weno5}
    horizontal: {type: weno5}
  riemann-solver: {type: lmars}
integration: {type: rk3, cfl: 0.9}   # three stages; the phase solve runs after the third
```

**What is refused, and why.**

1. *A legacy row layout.* Compiling with `NMASS>0` stops at the `static_assert` in `src/snap.h`
   ({{< code src/snap.h >}}) with "species rows must start right after the 5 hydro rows; NMASS>0 is not
   supported". Every species count in the EOS is `size - ICY`, which holds only when the species rows follow
   the five hydro rows.
2. *A stage outside the integrator.* `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` refuses a stage index outside
   $[0,N_{\mathrm{stage}})$ with "Invalid stage: " and the index, before it touches the state.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| face products and divergence | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}} | `dflx` | |
| face-area slice | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl::face_area1 >}} | `face_area1` | |
| flux-only increment | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `du` | |
| implicit correction | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `dt_corr` | `implicit-scheme`[^rg-4c9e26614577] |
| stage order and last stage | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `apply_boundaries` | |
| row layout | {{< code src/snap.h >}} | `ICY` | |

: Code map of the conservation laws and the stage order. {#tbl-ch02-laws-code}

**The excerpt.** The $x_1$ part of `CoordinateImpl::divergence` and the start of the increment in
`HydroImpl::forward`:

```cpp
dflx.slice(DIM1, si, ei) +=
    face_area1(si + 1, ei + 1) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si + 1, ei + 1) -
    face_area1(si, ei) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si, ei);
// ...
return dflx / vol;

auto du = torch::zeros_like(_div);
auto interior = pmb->part({0, 0, 0}, PartOptions().exterior(false));
du.index(interior) = -dt * _div.index(interior);
```

The two products are $[A\mathbf F_1]_{i+1/2}$ and $[A\mathbf F_1]_{i-1/2}$, formed separately from the same
area and flux tensors, so a face's product in its two cells is the same number (step 1); `dflx / vol` is the division by
$V_i$; the last line is @eq-ch02-laws-increment on interior cells, with ghosts left at zero.

The check is independent algebra plus a numpy port of the increment.[^laws-run] `[C1]`: four cells with
unequal volumes telescope with residual 0. `[C2]`: sympy confirms the six-cell sum leaves only the outer faces.
`[C3]`: over 200 random rows of 32 cells, the exact-arithmetic defect of the float64 increment is at most 0.304
of the derived bound.

The ctest case runs on CPU[^rg-d5c518c05d4f] and CUDA[^rg-6f633b2ccc44] where available, one rank. It has not been run for this report at the pin:

### Limits

1. **Limiters and sources change the budget.** The conserved limiter and the forcing modules add or remove mass
   and energy by design; the telescoping statement covers the flux-only increment.
2. **No measured convergence order** for the complete stage is given here; @sec-ch04 and @sec-ch07 own the
   spatial and temporal orders.
3. **Untested combinations.** Switch-combination coverage is in @sec-ch12-matrix.
